html:
The Complex of Goguryeo Tombs is a group of about thirty tombs of kings and nobles of Goguryeo around Pyongyang and Nampo, in North Korea, from the time after King Jangsu moved the capital to Pyongyang in 427.

Many have painted walls. They show hunting on horseback, dances, wrestling, kitchens and processions, and later the four guardian beasts of the directions: the blue dragon, white tiger, red bird and black tortoise. The paintings are the best record of how the Goguryeo nobility lived and believed, mixing local ideas with Buddhism and Chinese cosmology.

One of the tombs is said to be that of Dongmyeong, Goguryeo's founder. In 2004 the complex became North Korea's first World Heritage Site, with matching tombs on the Chinese side of the Yalu. Goguryeo's armies in this age defeated the Sui at the Salsu River.
